We've attached a small sample of errors and the request IDs we used to correlate (helix-503-sample.txt). Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood service incident, and whether HelixPay is eligible for SLA credit / account remedy? We also need a post-incident timeline and a short RCA for our compliance team.

- req_3a7b4c

Appreciate a quick confirmation — our UTC team is on standby.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 503s — preliminary findings

Sofia / team — preliminary SRE findings attached. We correlated the request IDs Marcus provided against our ingress logs and internal routing traces. Observations: 
- Confirmed a spike in 5xx responses for the customer in the window 2027-09-20T03:02:00Z–2027-09-20T03:40:00Z. Error-rate peaked at ~7.8% for that customer key.
- Root cause (preliminary): a partial control-plane failover in the us-west-2 serving cluster triggered an elevated error-return path for in-flight connections while a routing mesh redistributed KV caches.
- During the window we saw increased tail latency (p95 to p99 delta) and a temporary throttling policy mis-application on a subset of endpoints.

I’ve attached an SRE digest with request trace snippets and the service-side metric series: sre-digests.tar.gz (contains ingress-20270920.jsonl, trace-reqs.csv). To finish the RCA we need:
- confirmation of the exact customer_id used by HelixPay (to ensure we pulled all correlated requests)
- any client-side retry windows (to estimate retry amplification)

Preliminary credit calc: assuming their overall availability drop for the billing period exceeds the contractual threshold, the incident would qualify for a prorated remedy. For the 39-minute window and the measured drop we estimate a provisional remedial credit of ~3.2% of monthly invoice for impacted service usage, pending formal audit.

Next steps: I will stage the raw logs into the evidence bundle for HP-9876 and coordinate with Support for a public-facing timeline.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks, SRE

Marcus — thanks for the customer_id and the CSV. We have everything we need to complete the audit. Summary and commitments: 

What we validated (prelim):
- SRE confirmed a service-side anomaly in us-west-2 that produced the error spike for helix-corp-42 from 2027-09-20T03:02:00Z–2027-09-20T03:40:00Z.
- The behavior aligns with a control-plane failover and transient routing mismatch while caches were reconstructing.

What you’ll get next:
- Credit eligibility: We will complete the formal SLA calculation within 3 business days and provide a provisional credit percentage. If eligible, the credit will be applied as an account invoice credit on your next billing cycle; we’ll include the calculation sheet in the HP-9876 evidence bundle.
- Postmortem / RCA: SRE will publish a concise RCA (timeline, root cause, mitigation and actions) within 10 business days. If you need an earlier interim summary for compliance we can provide a 1–2 page timeline within 48 hours.
- Evidence bundle: will include raw ingress logs, trace snippets, and the correlated request IDs you provided (attachments: helix-503-sample.txt, helix-500-ids.csv, sre-digests.tar.gz).

- Dylan to finalize RCA and credit calc (SRE).

- Sofia / Aditya to shepherd the credit once SRE confirms and to update HP-9876.
